new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for Wogamusin, so nothing to agree with or contradict; this is the first placement statement found: fixed final stress, second-hand (van Zanten & Dol 2010 coding Laycock 1965a). The listed work itself, Goedemans's Australian chapter, is not about this language; the citation appears to have been attached to woga1249 by mistake (its Miriwung note is for an Australian language). Consistent with the second-hand facts already in : Laycock 1965: 114 (via Wikipedia) says schwa 'appears only in unstressed syllables' (a stress language) and Laycock assumed Wogamusin is not tonal (via Donohue 1997).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Van Zanten & Dol (2010, ch. 4 of the held volume) classify 'Wagamusin' with StressTyp code U, defined in the volume's code appendix as primary stress always on the final (ultimate) syllable; it is one of the three plain-U languages among their 51 'pure' stress Papuan languages (Table 2, p. 117: Dani, Wagamusin, Weri). The row is a bare code: the name is printed in italics (font check on p. 168: same italic font as the legend word 'italics' and as Abau/Abelam/Abun), i.e. NOT in the StressTyp database, and starred, i.e. not discussed anywhere in the chapter text; the only Wogamusin source in their reference list is Laycock 1965a, so the code is their reading of Laycock 1965a (still unread by us). Goedemans's own chapter (pp. 55-85, Australian languages) says nothing about Wogamusin; the 'Miriwung = no. 51' note in the citation is the Australian language Miriwung on his stress map key (p. 66).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Caveats: the classification is second-hand (a database code, no prose, no examples), the language is not in StressTyp itself, and the chapter warns that 33 of its 74 sample languages were 'added from any literature we could lay our hands on' (p. 116).
new_statements.identity_note: Van Zanten & Dol spell the language 'Wagamusin' (as does Laycock's 1965 title) and place it in 'Wagamusin Family, Sepik-River Phylum, Upper Sepik area, PNG' (Wurm 1982 classification); this is Glottolog woga1249 Wogamusin [wog] (Sepik; Iwam-Wogamus), villages Kubkain/Washkuk area. No dialect is specified.
